title: hostedapi-stream-silencing-fallback-notes-2026-07-03
content:
Summary:

This doc collects on-call notes and a draft runbook following a P0 window (2026-07-03 03:14–04:05 UTC) where a subset of hosted API streaming sessions experienced silent periods (no tokens from model) despite open connections. Affected tenants saw TTFB spikes to >10s, a rise in 5xx for stream writes, and increased session reconnects. The incident surfaced as customer reports of long pauses mid-stream and automated alerts for streaming session error rate.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture timeline from on-call shift and early SRE hypotheses
- Propose an interim fallback runbook to reduce customer impact while we root-cause
- List telemetry improvements and next-step engineering tasks

High-level impact:
- 12% of streaming sessions in us-central/edge-pop-4 experienced >3s inter-token gaps during the window.
- 18 customer-facing incidents (support) opened, 7 escalated to SEs.
- No data loss observed (sessions resumed), but UX degraded significantly for real-time apps.

Quick triage notes (on-call chronology):
- 03:14 UTC: Pager alert — streaming error budget breached (p99 inter-token gap).
- 03:16 UTC: Pager on-call (Priya) begins investigation, triangulates with edge-proxy errors (TLS handshakes with ticket-rotation failures), and increases in edge CPU.
- 03:22 UTC: Noted pattern: affected sessions anchored to a small set of edge hosts (edge-pop-4-bish).
- 03:28 UTC: Rolling restart of edge-proxy on edge-pop-4-bish reduced 5xx count but did not eliminate silent gaps.
- 03:37 UTC: Hypothesis formed: interplay between TLS ticket rotation + acceptor thread backpressure causing stream pollers to stall intermittently.
- 03:45 UTC: Canary fallback enabled: route streaming traffic from edge-pop-4-bish to adjacent pop (edge-pop-5) via smart-routing rule; p99 gaps improved within 90s for routed traffic.
- 03:52 UTC: Autoscaler logs show a brief spike of instance churn tied to scale-down attempts concurrent with ticket rotation window.
- 04:05 UTC: Incident moved to postmortem; support notified customers of mitigation (routing fallback) and monitoring continued.

Telemetry and signals inspected:
- edge-proxy logs: sustained WARNs around TLS ticket verification timeouts and occasional EAGAIN on acceptor sockets.
- host metrics: edge-pop-4-bish node set CPU at 85–95% for 2–3 minutes during spike; context-switch rate elevated.
- tracing: saw long tail between client-frame-received and dispatcher-enqueue times (suggests local stall).
- scheduler/acceptor: backlog transiently increased beyond configured thresholds leading to delayed session task handoff.
- autoscaler events: scale-down pulse at 03:40 that removed 1 of 3 edge instances; scale-down decision coincided with ticket rotation.

Root cause hypothesis (multi-factor):
- Primary: TLS ticket rotation on a small subset of edge hosts induced short, synchronized stalls in the edge-proxy TLS handshake path. Some acceptor threads hit locked IO paths and increased request scheduling latency.
- Secondary contributing factor: aggressive autoscaler scale-down policy removed a warm instance during the ticket rotation window, amplifying queueing pressure on remaining hosts.
- Tertiary: current fallback routing policy would not trigger until error thresholds (5xx) crossed; silent stream gaps (no 5xx) did not trip the route change quickly.

Why this combination produced the observed symptoms:
- TLS rotation is cheap but can cause microdelays if acceptor threads reinitialize locks simultaneously. With reduced instance count capacity, those microdelays translated into visible inter-token gaps rather than brief handshakes.
- Silent stalls only surfaced in streaming because the streaming code path relies on very low-latency continuous writes; no explicit response code is returned so 5xx thresholds remained low.

Immediate mitigations taken (what helped):
- Manual routing fallback to adjacent POP (edge-pop-5) for affected customers — immediate p99 improvement for routed sessions.
- Rolling restart of edge-proxy processes on the affected hosts — reduced error noise but did not fix root cause.
- Temporarily paused autoscaler scale-down for edge-pop-4 during immediate recovery window.

Draft runbook: short-term (playbook to run during recurrence)
1) Detection:
   - Alert: streaming-intertoken-gap-p99 > 2s in a POP for 3m
2) Initial triage (5m):
   - Check edge-pop CPU, acceptor backlog, and TLS ticket rotation timestamps (edge-proxy metrics).
   - If TLS ticket rotation correlated and >30% of edge nodes show WARN timeouts, proceed to 3.
3) Fast mitigation (10–20m):
   - Pause any in-progress scale-downs for that POP (autoscaler: pause-policy POP:<pop-id>).
   - Apply routing override to steer streaming traffic away from suspect POP to adjacent POP(s) (console -> smart-routing -> add override). Keep override for minimum 10m and observe.
   - Restart edge-proxy processes gracefully (rolling, 1 host at a time).
4) Escalation (if mitigation fails within 20m):
   - Route all streaming traffic off the POP and open an incident bridge.
   - Pager escalation to on-call SRE and networking guild.

Runbook Notes / Playbook rationale:
- We prefer routing over immediate full POP shutdown to preserve non-streaming traffic locality and reduce blast radius.
- Pausing scale-down prevents warm instance loss during transient doorstops like ticket rotation.

Proposed longer-term engineering tasks (owners assigned):
- (eng-proxy) decouple TLS ticket rotation from acceptor lock — investigate async rotation path. Owner: Liam Chen. Target: design + small prototype by 2026-08-01.
- (infra/autoscaler) implement safety check: avoid scale-down during known maintenance windows or when TLS rotation heatmap shows >X% hosts in rotation. Owner: Marisol Ortega. Target: 2026-07-24.
- (routing) reduce dependency on 5xx thresholds for streaming route failover; add latency-gap metric trigger. Owner: Omar Haddad. Target: 2026-07-17.
- (observability) add inter-token-gap histograms per POP and correlate with ticket-rotation events. Owner: eng-sre observability subteam. Target: 2026-07-10.

Follow-ups and action items (short list):
- [Priya] Draft customer-facing post-incident note for support to use (due 2026-07-11).
- [Liam] Post design doc for non-blocking TLS rotation (due 2026-07-01).
- [Marisol] Autoscaler quick-fix to pause scale-downs by POP (hotfix) and deploy to prod canary (due 2026-07-14).
- [Omar] Adjust routing rules to accept inter-token-gap signal (due 2026-07-17).

Metrics to monitor post-change:
- p50/p95/p99 inter-token gap per POP
- edge-proxy acceptor queue length and context-switch rate
- scale-down events per POP and timestamps relative to ticket rotations
- cross-pop routing events and customer impact after rule changes

Unresolved questions / hypothesis tests:
- Is TLS ticket rotation scheduling correlated cluster-wide by default, or did edge-proxy hosts synchronize in this case? (If synchronized, need jittering strategy.)
- Was there any edge-proxy memory pressure or GC that exacerbated stalls?
- Can we reproduce locally by forcing ticket rotation + artificial scale-down?

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Support saw chatty incident descriptions — keep customer comms short and focused: what we saw, what we mitigated, next steps.
- Add a small synthetic streaming probe that measures inter-token gap without relying on client behaviour — useful Canary.
